title: Argon ion speed
description: Essential: The student must correctly calculate the argon ion's speed entering the electric field using energy conservation: v0 = sqrt(2*q1*U0/m1) = 1.0e5 m/s.

title: Height difference A-M
description: Essential: The student must correctly determine the vertical drop from A to M (0.5 m) using kinematics in the uniform downward electric field.

title: Metal ion trajectory radius
description: Important: The student must correctly apply the Lorentz force law to find the radius of the metal ion's circular motion in the magnetic field: R = (m2*v)/(B*q2) = 0.5 m.

title: Geometry of deposition region
description: Important: The student must correctly analyze the geometry relating the circular arcs, the substrate line, and the given distance from M to the substrate to find the coated length.

title: Final coated length
description: Essential: The student must provide the final numerical answer for the length of the coated region on the substrate: (2 - sqrt(2))/2 m.

title: Kinematics setup
description: Important: The student must set up the horizontal and vertical kinematic equations for the argon ion's projectile motion in the electric field, linking time, distance, and acceleration.

title: Trigonometry application
description: Optional: The student correctly uses trigonometry (e.g., 45° angles) to relate distances in the geometry of the magnetic field regions and the substrate.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: The student makes a sign error in the electric force direction or confuses the orientation of the circular motion in the opposite magnetic fields.

title: Unit inconsistency
description: Pitfall: The student uses inconsistent units (e.g., not converting kV to V) or omits units in final answers.
